headline: CBA's own summary: operating income rose 6% (6.2%) to $30,224m, operating performance (pre-provision profit) rose 6% (6.5%) to $16,469m, and cash NPAT from continuing operations increased $730m or 7% to $10,982m from $10,252m (ev-1, ev-63, ev-65, ev-4, ev-7, ev-10, ev-67, ev-81). Statutory NPAT moved slightly differently: continuing-operations statutory NPAT rose $778m or 8% to $10,911m, while statutory NPAT including discontinued operations rose $750m or 7% to $10,866m (ev-8, ev-11). CBA calls statutory NPAT "broadly in line with Cash NPAT" (ev-78); the non-cash items separating them are transaction costs/(losses) on disposals (-$172m FY25, -$17m FY26) and hedging and IFRS volatility (+$53m FY25, -$54m FY26) (ev-75, ev-76). The bridge is fully closed with no residual: NII +$1,563m and other operating income +$196m, less underlying opex -$719m, notable items -$40m, loan impairment -$62m and tax -$208m. ROE rose to 14.0%; NIM fell 3bpts to 2.05% but was stable ex-liquids (ev-79, ev-19, ev-20).

drivers.narrative: NII $25,586m, up $1,563m or 7%, driven by AIEA +$92bn/+8% to $1,246bn, partly offset by NIM -3bpts to 2.05%; ex-liquids NIM was "stable". Average lending IEA +$60bn/+7%: home loans +$32bn/+5% to $630bn, business/corporate +$27bn/+10% to $299bn (Business Banking, institutional and structured lending).

drivers.narrative: Within NII: NIM fell 3bpts to 2.05% (2.08% FY25). Asset pricing cost 5bpts — home lending pricing -4bpts, business/institutional -1bpt — "primarily reflecting the impact of competition"; portfolio mix added 2bpts from business-lending asset mix and deposit funding mix; funding costs and basis risk flat. Liquids growth is "broadly neutral" to NII.

Other operating income $4,638m, +$196m/+4%. Commissions +$135m to $2,234m (higher insurance income incl. a CommInsure General Insurance sale milestone payment, equities income, syndication fees; offset by deposit-fee waivers, lower card fees from higher loyalty costs, lower FX). Other income +$46m to $156m (Gemini IPO fair-value gain, minorities; offset by lower Structured Asset Finance after the aircraft lease sale). Lending fees +$12m, funds management +$12m, trading -$9m to $1,190m.

UNDERLYING (ex notable items) opex $13,585m, +$719m/+6% (5.6%); headline opex +5.8%. CBA's own primary walk: inflation +$455m, investment in technology +$444m, investment in frontline and operations +$128m, other +$96m, productivity -$404m. By line: IT services +$393m/+16% to $2,782m (cloud, software licensing, AI/resilience); staff +$288m/+4% to $8,258m (average FTE +1,760 to 51,756); other +$57m; occupancy -$19m.

Notable items rose $40m (31%) from $130m to $170m. FY26: provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment to certain customers from ASIC's Better Banking review; domestic customer remediation. FY25: domestic ($52m) and NZ ($33m) remediation plus a $45m Bankwest restructuring provision. CBA does not publish a per-item split of the FY26 $170m. All $170m fell in 1H26; nil in 2H26.

LIE $788m, up $62m or 9% (8.5%); LIE/average GLAA +1bpt to 8bpts. Retail Banking Services +$106m to $378m (geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty, cost-of-living) and New Zealand +$11m to $66m (unemployment outlook), partly offset by Business Banking -$45m to $310m (lower individually assessed charges, more write-backs) and Institutional Banking and Markets -$16m to $33m (release of individual provisions).

Corporate tax expense $4,699m, up $208m or 5% on higher pre-tax profit. The effective cash tax rate FELL 50bpts from 30.5% to 30.0%, "primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses" — so the rate was a partial offset to the volume-driven rise in tax paid. CBA guides ~30% for FY27.

disagreements.explanation: Identical dollar levels ($30,224m / $13,585m against $28,465m / $12,866m); the slide simply prints one decimal place. The slide also adds headline opex growth of +5.8% including notable items (ev-69).

Statutory grew faster because FY25 carried a larger non-cash drag (-$172m disposals incl. a $222m Bank of Hangzhou loss, offset by +$53m hedging) than FY26 (-$17m disposals, -$54m hedging) (ev-75, ev-76). These items explain the same-period statutory/cash gap, not the year-on-year cash movement, so they are excluded from the bridge.

Appendix 1.5 is labelled 'Total net other operating income - statutory basis' and includes hedging ineffectiveness and disposal losses (e.g. the FY25 $222m Bank of Hangzhou loss) that cash basis excludes. The cash-basis table on p14 is the correct input to a cash-earnings bridge.

limitations: The bank publishes no single cash-NPAT waterfall for FY26 vs FY25; the bridge is assembled from the Group Performance Summary table (ev-1 to ev-7) plus each component's own stated 'on the prior year' movement. Every component is a bank-stated movement or a bank-published primary walk bar, and the six components sum exactly to the $730m movement, leaving a zero residual.

NII is claimed as a single total. CBA does not split the $1,563m into dollar volume and margin effects; the volume (+$92bn AIEA) and margin (-3bpts) drivers are disclosed only in units, so nii.margin is carried as an unquantified-in-dollars driver with its bps detail.

The NIM walk on p28 (Liquids -0.02, Asset pricing -0.05, Funding costs 0.00, Portfolio mix +0.02, Basis risk 0.00, Capital/Replicating and Other, Treasury & Markets) is printed in percentage points, not dollars, and its bars could not be paired to labels via the chart reader; the bps figures used are those CBA states in the accompanying narrative text.

CBA qualifies the NIM move: liquid-asset growth has 'broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' and ex-liquids NIM was 'stable' (ev-20), so the headline -3bpts overstates the economic margin pressure on the NII bar.

The $170m FY26 notable items figure is not broken into per-item amounts (NZ legal settlement, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment, domestic remediation); only the FY25 $130m is itemised ($52m/$33m/$45m). The $40m delta is therefore attributable in total but not by sub-item.

The tax contribution is the movement in tax EXPENSE (-$208m). It nets a volume effect (higher pre-tax profit) against a favourable 50bpt fall in the effective rate; CBA does not disclose the dollar split between the two.

The productivity bar (-$404m) in the expense walk is a net offset within a gross expense increase; CBA also cites 'favourable FX' as an offset across staff, occupancy and other expenses without quantifying it.

All figures are continuing-operations basis. Cash NPAT including discontinued operations is $10,982m FY26 vs $10,253m FY25 ($1m of FY25 discontinued cash profit), a $729m movement — immaterially different from the $730m continuing-operations bridge.
Capped at 80: notable_items -40 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

Cash net profit after tax (cash NPAT or cash profit) from continuing operations increased $730 million or 7% on the prior year to $10,982 million. The result was driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2, as well as a $62 million increase in loan impairment expense.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased 7%, primarily driven by an 8% or $92 billion increase in Average Interest Earning Assets (AIEA). Excluding the impact of liquid assets, underlying Net Interest Margin (NIM) was stable. Average lending interest earning assets increased by $60 billion or 7% due to growth in home, business and institutional lending.

Underlying NIM was supported by higher earnings on replicating portfolio and capital hedges, and favourable portfolio mix, offset by the impact of increased lending price competition and Treasury and Markets.

Other operating income increased 4% primarily driven by higher insurance income and the benefit of one-off gains 3, higher volume driven equities income, partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue following the sale of the aircraft lease portfolio, lower foreign exchange income, lower deposit fees due to fee waivers and lower credit card fees from higher loyalty costs.
